#### Before the primaries

Media speculation had begun almost immediately after the results of the [2004 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election "2004 United States presidential election") were released. In the [2006 midterm elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_United_States_elections "2006 United States elections"), the Democrats regained majorities in both houses of the [U.S. Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-7) Early polls taken before anyone had announced a candidacy had shown Senators [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton") and [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") as the most popular potential Democratic candidates.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-guardian-2006-8) Nevertheless, the media speculated on several other candidates, including [Al Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore"), the runner-up in the [2000 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election "2000 United States presidential election"); [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry"), the runner-up in the [2004 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election "2004 United States presidential election"); [John Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Edwards "John Edwards"), Kerry's [running mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_mate "Running mate") in 2004; Delaware Senator [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"); New Mexico Governor [Bill Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Richardson "Bill Richardson"); Iowa Governor [Tom Vilsack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Vilsack "Tom Vilsack"); and Indiana Senator [Evan Bayh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Bayh "Evan Bayh").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-CSM-9)

Edwards was one of the first to formally announce his candidacy for the presidency, on December 28, 2006. This run would be his second attempt at the presidency.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-10) Clinton announced intentions to run in the Democratic primaries on January 20, 2007.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-11) Obama announced his candidacy on February 10 in his home state of Illinois.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-12)

#### Early primaries and caucuses

Early in the year, the support for Barack Obama started to increase in the polls and he passed Clinton for the top spot in Iowa; he ended up winning the caucus in that state, with Edwards coming in second and Clinton in third.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-Iowa-13) Obama's win was fueled mostly by first time caucus-goers and [Independents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_(voter) "Independent (voter)") and showed voters viewed him as the "candidate of change".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-Iowa-13) Iowa has since been viewed as the state that jump-started Obama's campaign and set him on track to win both the nomination and the presidency.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-14) After the [Iowa caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Iowa_Democratic_presidential_caucuses "2008 Iowa Democratic presidential caucuses"), Biden and Connecticut Senator [Chris Dodd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Dodd "Chris Dodd") withdrew from the nomination contest.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-Iowa-13)

Obama became the new front runner in New Hampshire, when his poll numbers skyrocketed after his Iowa victory.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-New_Hampshire_polls-15) The Clinton campaign was struggling after a huge loss in Iowa and no strategy beyond the early primaries and caucuses. According to _[The Vancouver Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vancouver\_Sun "The Vancouver Sun")_, campaign strategists had "mapped a victory scenario that envisioned the former first lady wrapping up the Democratic presidential nomination by Super Tuesday on Feb. 5."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-16) In what is considered a turning point for her campaign, Clinton had a strong performance at the [Saint Anselm College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Anselm_College "Saint Anselm College"), [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), and [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") debates several days before the [New Hampshire primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_New_Hampshire_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 New Hampshire Democratic presidential primary") as well as an emotional interview in a public broadcast live on TV.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-17) Clinton won that primary by 2% of the vote, contrary to the predictions of pollsters who consistently had her trailing Obama for a few days up to the primary date.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-New_Hampshire_polls-15) Clinton's win was the first time a woman had ever won a major American party's presidential primary for the purposes of delegate selection.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-ReferenceA-18)

On January 30, 2008, after placing in third in the New Hampshire and [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_South_Carolina_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 South Carolina Democratic presidential primary") primaries, Edwards announced that he was suspending his campaign for the presidency, but he did not initially endorse any remaining candidates.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-CBSend-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-20)

#### Super Tuesday

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Super_Tuesday_Vote_Utah.jpg/250px-Super_Tuesday_Vote_Utah.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Super_Tuesday_Vote_Utah.jpg)

Voting sign in Utah

[Super Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Tuesday,_2008 "Super Tuesday, 2008") was February 5, 2008, when the largest-ever number of simultaneous state [primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_primary "United States presidential primary") elections was held.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-SJFPPbbc-21) Super Tuesday ended up leaving the Democrats in a virtual tie, with Obama amassing 847 delegates to Clinton's 834 from the 23 states that held Democratic primaries.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-22)

[California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_California_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 California Democratic presidential primary") was one of the Super Tuesday states that could provide a large number of delegates to the candidates. Obama trailed in the California polling by an average of 6.0% before the primary; he ended up losing that state by 8.3% of the vote.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-fivethirtyeight1-23) Some analysts cited a large [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") turnout that voted for Clinton as the deciding factor.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-24)

The [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Louisiana_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Louisiana Democratic presidential primary"), [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Nebraska_Democratic_presidential_caucuses "2008 Nebraska Democratic presidential caucuses"), [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Hawaii_Democratic_presidential_caucuses "2008 Hawaii Democratic presidential caucuses"), [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Wisconsin_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Wisconsin Democratic presidential primary"), [U.S. Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_U.S._Virgin_Islands_Democratic_presidential_convention "2008 U.S. Virgin Islands Democratic presidential convention"), the [District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_District_of_Columbia_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 District of Columbia Democratic presidential primary"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Maryland_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Maryland Democratic presidential primary"), and [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Virginia_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Virginia Democratic presidential primary") primaries and the [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Democratic_caucuses,_2008 "Washington Democratic caucuses, 2008") and Maine caucuses all took place after Super Tuesday in February. Obama won all of them, giving him 10 consecutive victories after Super Tuesday.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-msnbc21660914-26)

#### Ohio, Texas, and Pennsylvania

On March 4, Hillary Clinton carried [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Ohio_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Ohio Democratic presidential primary") and [Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Rhode_Island_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Rhode Island Democratic presidential primary") in the Democratic primaries; some considered these wins, especially Ohio, a "surprise upset" by 10%,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-28) although she did lead in the polling averages in both states.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-fivethirtyeight1-23)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-SuperTuesdayIIresults-29) She also carried the [primary in Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Texas_Democratic_presidential_primary_and_caucuses "2008 Texas Democratic presidential primary and caucuses"), but Obama won the Texas caucuses held the same day and netted more delegates from the state than Clinton.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-30)

Only one state held a primary in April. This was [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Pennsylvania_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Pennsylvania Democratic presidential primary"), on April 22. Although Obama made a strong effort to win Pennsylvania, Hillary Clinton won that primary by nearly 10%, with approximately 55% of the vote.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-Clinton_Wins_PA-31) Obama had outspent Clinton three to one in Pennsylvania, but his comment at a San Francisco fundraiser that small-town Americans "cling" to guns and religion drew sharp criticism from the Clinton campaign and may have hurt his chances in the Keystone State.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-Guns_and_Religion-32) In addition, Clinton had several advantages in Pennsylvania. Throughout the primary process, she relied on the support of older, white, working class voters. Pennsylvania held a closed primary, which means that only registered Democrats could vote, and, according to Ron Elving of [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR"), the established Democratic electorate "was older, whiter, more Catholic and more working-class than in most of the primaries to date."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-33) After Pennsylvania, Obama had a higher number of delegates and popular votes than Clinton did and was still in a stronger position to win the nomination. Clinton, however, had received the endorsement of more superdelegates than Obama.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-Clinton_Wins_PA-31)

#### Indiana and North Carolina

On May 6, [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_North_Carolina_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 North Carolina Democratic presidential primary") and [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Indiana_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Indiana Democratic presidential primary") held their Democratic presidential primaries. Clinton and Obama campaigned aggressively there before the voting took place. Polling had shown Obama a few points ahead in North Carolina and Clinton similarly leading in Indiana.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-35) In the actual results, Obama outperformed the polls by several points in both states, winning by a significant margin in North Carolina[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-36) and losing by only 1.1% in Indiana (50.56% to 49.44%).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-37) After these primaries, most pundits declared that it had become "increasingly improbable," if not impossible, for Clinton to win the nomination.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-38) The small win in Indiana barely kept her campaign alive for the next month.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-39) Although she did manage to win the majority of the remaining primaries and delegates, it was not enough to overcome Obama's substantial delegate lead.

#### Florida and Michigan

During late 2007, the two parties adopted rules against states' moving their primaries to an earlier date in the year. For the Republicans, the penalty for this violation was supposed to be the loss of half the state party's delegates to the convention. The Democratic penalty was the complete exclusion from the national convention of delegates from states that broke these rules. The Democratic Party allowed only four states to hold elections before February 5, 2008. Clinton won a majority of delegates and popular votes from both states (though 40% voted uncommitted in Michigan) and subsequently led a fight to seat all the [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Florida_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Florida Democratic presidential primary") and [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Michigan_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Michigan Democratic presidential primary") delegates.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-40)

There was some speculation that the fight over the delegates could last until the convention in August. On May 31, 2008, the Rules and Bylaws Committee of the Democratic Party reached a compromise on the Florida and Michigan delegate situation. The committee decided to seat delegates from Michigan and Florida at the convention in August, but to only award each a half-vote.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-41)

#### Clinching the nomination

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/2008_DNC_during_Stevie_Wonder%27s_performance.jpg/250px-2008_DNC_during_Stevie_Wonder%27s_performance.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008_DNC_during_Stevie_Wonder's_performance.jpg)

2008 DNC during Stevie Wonder's performance

The major political party nomination process (technically) continues through June of an election year. In previous cycles, the candidates were effectively chosen by the end of the primaries held in March, but, in this cycle, Barack Obama did not win enough delegates to secure the nomination until June 3, after a 17-month campaign against Hillary Clinton. He had a wide lead in states won, while Clinton had won majorities in several of the larger states. Now, because a form of [proportional representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proportional_representation "Proportional representation") and popular vote decided Democratic state delegate contests, numbers were close between Clinton and Obama.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-42) By May, Clinton claimed to hold a lead in the popular vote, but the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") found that her numbers were "accurate only" in one close scenario.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-43)

In June, after the last of the primaries had taken place, Obama secured the Democratic nomination for president, with the help of multiple super delegate endorsements (most of the super delegates had refused to declare their support for either candidate until the primaries were completed).[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-44) He was the first African American to win the nomination of a major political party in the United States.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-45) For several days, Clinton refused to concede the race, although she signaled her presidential campaign was ending in a post-primary speech on June 3 in her home state of New York.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-46) She finally conceded the nomination to Obama on June 7. She pledged her full support to the [presumptive nominee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presumptive_nominee_(United_States) "Presumptive nominee (United States)") and vowed to do everything she could to help him get elected.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-47) Clinton would eventually become the Democratic presidential nominee [8 years later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election"), which she then lost the general election to [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump").

### Republican Party

Main articles: [John McCain 2008 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain_2008_presidential_campaign "John McCain 2008 presidential campaign"), [2008 Republican Party presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2008 Republican Party presidential primaries"), and [2008 Republican National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Republican_National_Convention "2008 Republican National Convention")

Not only was the 2008 election the first time since [1952](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_United_States_presidential_election "1952 United States presidential election") that neither the [incumbent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incumbent "Incumbent") president nor the incumbent vice president was a candidate in the general election, but it was also the first time since the [1928 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_United_States_presidential_election "1928 United States presidential election") that neither sought his party's nomination for president; as Bush was term-limited from seeking another nomination, the unique aspect was Vice President Cheney's decision not to seek the Republican nomination.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-harnden2007-48)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-artandhistory1925-49) The 2008 election was also the third presidential election since [1896](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_United_States_presidential_election "1896 United States presidential election") in which neither the incumbent president, the incumbent vice president, nor a current or former member of the incumbent president's [Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States") won the nomination of either major party the others being [1920](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_United_States_presidential_election "1920 United States presidential election") and [1952](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_United_States_presidential_election "1952 United States presidential election").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-cjones1-50) With no members of the Bush administration emerging as major contenders for the Republican nomination, the Republican race was as open as the Democratic race.
